critical_code_review_comments: FreshnessBadge picks the MAX last_import_at across all sources. This is user-friendly for the summary chip, but a stale-but-critical source (e.g. open_documents 3 days old) will be masked when a fresher unrelated import (client_info) exists. Consider surfacing the MIN date (worst source) or an aggregated per-source hover for the tooltip to avoid a false sense of freshness in mixed-cadence scenarios.

Login response payload does not include finance_role in the user object (RBAC enforced correctly server-side, but frontend can't sidebar-gate purely from login data — currently gating works via 403 responses on protected calls or via /users/me if used). If UI relies on user.finance_role client-side, confirm it is fetched elsewhere (e.g. an /auth/me follow-up) or add it to the login response.

WhatsApp kill-switch returns 503 on /webhook and 404 on undefined GETs — mixed semantics. Consider unifying to 404 (behaves like the route doesn't exist) when WHATSAPP_ENABLED=false, so external probes cannot infer the module exists but is disabled. Not blocking.
